# [TASK] Replace Alan AI voice control with self-hosted speech-to-text

## Task

Alan AI (the third-party voice SDK) stopped working — the hardcoded project key can't reach Alan's servers anymore (dead project on their side, confirmed via endless failed reconnects in console logs, not a bug in our code). Replace it with a self-hosted pipeline: browser mic -> local speech-to-text -> command handling, instead of a third-party SDK.

Chose self-hosted speech-to-text over the browser's built-in Speech Recognition API (faster to ship, but depends on Chrome/Google's servers) for $0 cost, no silently-dying third-party dependency, and a stronger showcase feature.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] ai-service exposes a working speech-to-text endpoint, reachable end-to-end via browser -> gateway -> ai-service (#69 fixed
      (`SpeechToTextServiceTest`)
- [x] Frontend captures mic audio and gets a transcription back — verified by the user in a real browser
- [x] All 4 existing voice commands work end-to-end (genre browsing, dark/light mode toggle, logout, search) — user confirmed live
- [x] `@alan-ai/alan-sdk-web` removed from `package.json` — confirmed, no remaining references anywhere in `frontend/filmpire`
- [x] No cloud cost — runs entirely on the local stack (Vosk model, no API key)

## Estimate

**Hours:** 10

## Notes

- Approach: `SpeechToTextService` (ai-service) loads a Vosk model lazily; audio is resampled server-side to mono 16kHz PCM16; `VoiceControl.jsx` (frontend) replaces the old `Alan.jsx`, re-encoding mic audio to WAV in-browser before upload; `voiceCommands.js` keyword-matches the transcribed text into the same command shape Alan's `onCommand` used to produce.
- Do not close on direct-backend testing alone — this was closed once before on that basis, which missed the browser -> gateway -> ai-service routing bug (#69). Now verified through the real path.
- Commits: `2932e21`, `9edcc0a`.
